about.title: about
about.paragraph_1: the total installation “l63” records the transition of gleaming metal into decomposition. a patinated path spreading across sheets of brass moves like a virus, creating an anomaly. yet destruction does not erase traces—it creates them. the black path embodies movement transformed into an imprint of living memory. this is not a line of disappearance but a line of transformation in which material and immaterial merge: the power of objecthood over space, the exhumation of material from the world of brass.
about.paragraph_2: material is not merely a physical substance but also the process of its transformation. the brass sheets reflecting light create an illusion of stability, yet inevitably enter into dialogue with decay. blackness penetrates the structure, deforms the material’s surface, and absorbs its shine, leaving behind distorted “matter.” this process is not simply disintegration but a kind of transmutation: matter changes state, revealing the tension between disappearance and the emergence of something new.
